key_big: A number bond shows a whole and two parts. The two parts make the whole.
body_html:
What is a number bond?

A number bond shows a whole and two parts.

The whole goes in the top circle. The parts go in the circles below.

The two parts make the whole.

Number bonds to 10

WholeParts
101 and 9
102 and 8
103 and 7
104 and 6
105 and 5

Number bonds to 20

A number from 11 to 20 is 10 and some more.

Example

What is the missing part? Whole 13, one part 8.

Count on from 8: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13. That is 5. 8 + 5 = 13.

Answer: 5

Fact family

One number bond gives four number sentences.

Example

Siti has 12 sweets. 7 are red. The rest are green. How many are green?

12 is 7 and 5. 12 − 7 = 5.

Answer: 5 green sweets

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Whole 10, part 4: “the missing part is 14”Do not add the whole and a part. 10 is 4 and 6
6 + 5 = 106 + 5 = 11. The partner of 6 in 10 is 4
Putting the whole in a bottom circleThe whole is the biggest number. It goes on top
Counting 8, 9, 10, 11 to get 4 for 8 + □ = 11Do not count the 8. Say 9, 10, 11. That is 3

faq.q: What is a number bond in P1 maths?
faq.a: A number bond shows how a whole splits into two parts, such as 10 is 7 and 3. Primary 1 students use number bonds to add and subtract within 20.

faq.q: How do I teach number bonds to my child?
faq.a: Start with real things, like 8 buttons split into two groups. Then draw the circles and ask which part is missing. A few minutes a day helps.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with number bonds?
faq.a: Many children add the whole and a part, so whole 10 and part 4 gives 14. Remind them that the parts are smaller than the whole.

faq.q: Are number bonds in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. The MOE Primary 1 syllabus teaches addition and subtraction with number bonds and the link between them. They are also used later for mental maths.
